title: Leopold Aschenbrenner explains where to invest for the next big 3 year AI trade His Q3 investor letter says the market is underestimating the speed AI moves from chatbots to agents to superintelligence He expects 2027 to pack 3 years of AI progress into 1 ye
title_en:
Leopold Aschenbrenner explains where to invest for the next big 3 year AI trade

His Q3 investor letter says the market is underestimating the speed AI moves from chatbots to agents to superintelligence

He expects 2027 to pack 3 years of AI progress into 1 year

his letter focuses around these companies/stocks:

• Foundation Models: Anthropic is the main bet because the model itself becomes the product. Situational Awareness LP (SALP) says Anthropic ARR grew ~80x in 22 months, from ~$1B to ~$81B, and argues leading AI labs could exit 2027 at $1T+ combined revenue run-rate

• Memory Chip Supply: SK Hynix, Kioxia, and SanDisk benefit if long-running AI agents make memory and storage more valuable. Leopold says reinforcement learning and agents make AI chips limited by memory, which is why he viewed Hynix as a $100B company that could become a $1T company

• GPU Rentals: SpaceX, Nebius, SharonAI, CoreWeave, and IREN benefit if AI labs keep renting short-term GPU capacity at higher prices. SALP says an H100 used to earn ~$1-$2/hour, now earns ~$5-$10/hour, and could reach $100s/hour+ if superintelligence demand hits

• Datacenter Power Supply: Bloom Energy benefits if AI datacenters pay more to get power online faster. AI buildout needs more than cheap power, it needs power immediately 

• Robotics: Robotics becomes the next major theme if AI starts doing real-world labor. Leopold says frontier models are starting to beat specialist robotics models, which means the next advancement may come from better AI models

Leopold warns software companies, AI wrappers, chip designers, and even today’s AI winners may lose their moats once AI can replace the engineers, code, IP, and management they are valued on

Stocks to own:

• Anthropic $ANT
• SK Hynix $SKHY
• Kioxia $KXIAY
• SanDisk $SNDK
• SpaceX $SPCX
• Nebius $NBIS
• SharonAI $SHAZ
• CoreWeave $CRWV
• IREN $IREN
• Bloom Energy $BE

Stocks to avoid:

• Salesforce $CRM
• Adobe $ADBE
• ServiceNow $NOW
• http://C3.ai $AI
• Synopsys $SNPS
• Arm $ARM
• Nvidia $NVDA
• AMD $AMD 
• Broadcom $AVGO
• ASML $ASML

他
author: @LeopoldTracker_
summary_zh:
的信主要围绕这些公司/股票：

• 基础模型：人择是主要选择，因为模型本身就成为了产品。 Situational Awareness LP (SALP) 表示，Anthropic ARR 在 22 个月内增长了约 80 倍，从约 $1B 增长到约 $81B，并认为领先的人工智能实验室可能会以 1T+ 的综合收入运行率退出 2027 年

• 内存芯片供应：如果长期运行的人工智能代理使内存和存储变得更有价值，SK Hynix、Kioxia 和 SanDisk 就会受益。 Leopold 表示，强化学习和代理使 AI 芯片受到内存的限制，这就是为什么他认为 Hynix 是一家 100B 美元的公司，可能会成为一家 1T 美元的公司

• GPU 租赁：如果人工智能实验室继续以更高的价格租赁短期 GPU 容量，SpaceX、Nebius、SharonAI、CoreWeave 和 IREN 就会受益。 SALP 表示，H100 过去每小时收入约为 1-2 美元，现在每小时收入约为 5-10 美元，如果超级智能需求达到，每小时可能会达到 100 美元以上

• 数据中心电源：如果人工智能数据中心支付更多费用以更快地获得电力，Bloom Energy 就会受益。人工智能建设需要的不仅仅是廉价电力，它还需要立即电力

• 机器人技术：如果人工智能开始从事现实世界的劳动，机器人技术将成为下一个主题。利奥波德表示，前沿模型开始击败专业机器人模型，这意味着下一个进步可能来自更好的人工智能模型

利奥波德警告说，一旦人工智能能够取代他们所重视的工程师、代码、IP和管理，软件公司、人工智能包装商、芯片设计师，甚至今天的人工智能获胜者都可能会失去护城河

title: Anthropic says Claude doesn't silently sabotage work and that some user reports reflect "overcaution", where Claude clings to self-imposed rules on long tasks (Edwin/@edwinarbus)
title_en:
Claude has not been trained to sabotage work. Yes, it sometimes makes mistakes, and other agents might identify them, but this isn’t sabotage.

There have been a few screenshots floating around of an outdated Fable 5 system card. For the first two days of Fable 5's launch in June, we did apply non-visible safeguards to some LLM research. This was a mistake, and we reversed it on June 10. These safeguards now clearly block the request or fall back, with a message users can see (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/refusals-and-fallback).

title: I am about 30 pages into the Q3 Situational Awareness letter. The full letter is 160 pages. All I can say so far is that if Leopold is right about where he sees AI going...the disconnect between market valuations across the AI stack and the level of growth we shoul
title_en:
I am about 30 pages into the Q3 Situational Awareness letter. The full letter is 160 pages.

All I can say so far is that if Leopold is right about where he sees AI going...the disconnect between market valuations across the AI stack and the level of growth we should expect is one of the largest disconnects we have ever seen in financial markets.

Some of these predictions are quite hard to believe, but I guess that's also the point of his fund. He writes, "Either we or the market will have an extraordinary amount of egg on the face in a year."

Will post deeper thoughts tomorrow after reading through the whole thing, the most interesting insights so far: he thinks the frontier labs will do $1T of ARR by end of 2027, a ChatGPT moment for Robotics will come by late 2027, and that RSI is significantly being discounted by the market which could end up becoming so strong that it could lead to the shutdown of all models by the government.

We are living in one of the craziest times to be an investor.
title_zh:
我已经读了大约 30 页的第三季度态势感知信函。整封信有160页。

到目前为止我能说的是，如果利奥波德对人工智能发展方向的看法是正确的……整个人工智能堆栈的市场估值与我们预期的增长水平之间的脱节是我们在金融市场上见过的最大脱节之一。

其
author: @amitisinvesting
summary_zh:
中一些预测相当令人难以置信，但我想这也是他的基金的意义所在。他写道：“无论是我们还是市场，一年内都会出现大量的鸡蛋。”

明天读完整篇文章后，我将发表更深入的想法，迄今为止最有趣的见解：他认为前沿实验室将在 2027 年底前完成 1T 美元的 ARR，机器人技术的 ChatGPT 时刻将在 2027 年底到来，而 RSI 正在被市场大幅打折，最终可能变得如此强劲，以至于可能导致政府关闭所有模型。

我们正生活在投资者最疯狂的时代之一。

title_en:
Google Gemini Neon is the best AI model on planet Earth right now

It's smarter, faster, and more token efficient

The issue is, most people don't know how to use Antigravity, the official Google harness

Here are the most important tips:

🔶 /swarm: this might be the most powerful skill in Antigravity. It allows you to tackle complex challenges with swarms of AI agents

If you have a complex challenge (like architecture planning for instance) that has many different possible solutions, use /swarm

🔶 /grill-me: lots of harnesses have /grill-me, but I like Antigravity's the best. Anytime you are in the beginning stages of building, run this skill. Antigravity will ask you TONS of questions to iron out your plan

🔶 Antigravity on mobile: Antigravity unfortunately has no mobile app. But you can still use it on mobile! Go to settings > Application> remote control. This will generate a link you can send to your phone so you can code as you go

🔶 Antigravity Deep Research: Google just open sourced their official deep research skill, and it's excellent. It's built for Neon and Antigravity. Ask your agent to download the deep-research skill from Google demo lab

🔶 Knowledge work interface: If you're using Neon more for knowledge work, there is a knowledge work UI in the settings to make the overall interface less technical. Try it out!

Feel free to come back to these and let me know any other tips you have!

title: Current Status: Helping my teenager with his computer science homework. He's taking an undergrad-level computer science class as a sophomore in high school. I'm having to dig in to the Racket programming language and functional programming (which I h
title_en:
Current Status: Helping my teenager with his computer science homework. He's taking an undergrad-level computer science class as a sophomore in high school.  

I'm having to dig in to the Racket programming language and functional programming (which I haven't had to do in 30+ years). Evidently they use it as a teaching language at Northeastern University (great school and program! -- lots of HubSpotters graduated from there).

On a related note, the "How To Design Programs" book (first edition available for free online) is really good.  

By the way, if you're wondering: "Is computer science even going to be relevant in a few years, given the advent of AI?", my answer is: "Yes, I think so."  I think the value of fundamental systems thinking skills and problem solving will continue to be relevant. We'll be working at a higher level of abstraction, but those that have the core skills will have an advantage in the new AI-era because their skills get amplified.

p.s. When you've been writing in Python for decades, it's hard to adjust one's brain to pure functional programming. Just let me write a loop!

title: I don’t know where this AI alpha debate came from but it seems inverted to me. The central risk of AI in markets is not that it eliminates alpha, but that it convinces more participants they have a reason to take risk in pursuit of alpha which leads to persistently hig
title_en: I don’t know where this AI alpha debate came from but it seems inverted to me. The central risk of AI in markets is not that it eliminates alpha, but that it convinces more participants they have a reason to take risk in pursuit of alpha which leads to persistently higher volatility. The highest value application of AI could be a daily alert telling you whether taking risk is warranted at all.
title_zh: 我不知道关于人工智能阿尔法的争论从何而来，但对我来说似乎是相反的。人工智能在市场中的主要风险不是它消除了阿尔法，而是它让更多参与者相信他们有理由冒险追求阿尔法，从而导致波动性持续上升。人工智能最有价值的应用可能是每日警报，告诉您是否值得冒险
author: @pmje73

title: our learnings from building proactive, multiplayer agents 🧵 agents in ando can now decide when to chime in ~60,000x faster: 9.1 µs locally vs ~560 ms with a hosted decision engine like jev the trick is a conformal gate - a tiny local model that learns from a host
title_en:
our learnings from building proactive, multiplayer agents 🧵

agents in ando can now decide when to chime in ~60,000x faster: 9.1 µs locally vs ~560 ms with a hosted decision engine like jev

the trick is a conformal gate - a tiny local model that learns from a hosted teacher model & answers only when it can prove it's within its error budget
title_zh:
我们从构建主动的多人代理中学到的东西

ando 中的代理现在可以决定何时插话，速度提高了约 60,000 倍：本地 9.1 µs，而使用 jev 等托管决策引擎约 560 毫秒

诀窍是共形门 - 一个微小的本地模型，它从托管的教师模型中
author: @saradu
summary_zh: 学习，并且仅当它可以证明它在其错误预算之内时才给出答案

title: Update on NEAR Hackathon First, I apologize for the delay in communication and judging. We have had an overwhelming number of great submissions to the hackathon and it's amazing to see and congrats to everyone who participated! We live in amazing ti
title_en:
Update on NEAR Hackathon

First, I apologize for the delay in communication and judging. We have had an overwhelming number of great submissions to the hackathon and it's amazing to see and congrats to everyone who participated!

We live in amazing time where one can turn their ideas into working products with pure will and some agent back-and-forth.

The result still depends on the person who does it. Taste, knowledge, attention to detail and curious mind is what makes submissions stand out.

We wanted to see what you can build with NEAR's tech stack and your ingenuity and talent. And you have delivered: more than 2,500 projects and most importantly over 80% of them scored above our quality bar.

This is not how hackathons used to be. Two weeks is now enough to build a solid working product that is ready to be presented to users.

We used AI agents to judge too. Today, I'm publishing the shortlist of finalists, from which we will choose the winners.

Please look through it and tell us in the comments what you think, or point us to projects we may have missed. 

With this many submissions, mistakes are easy to make. So you can still influence our decision and make the case for your project.

For project details see nearhackathon(.)com

See you in the comments.

title: We can’t scale a negative gross margin business. That’s just impossible. Muse is a personal assistant, but doesn’t apply the level of heavy-hitter AI needed to operate a company at serious scale. If Grok Bots are providing high value on par with having excellen
title_en:
We can’t scale a negative gross margin business. That’s just impossible. 

Muse is a personal assistant, but doesn’t apply the level of heavy-hitter AI needed to operate a company at serious scale. 

If Grok Bots are providing high value on par with having excellent employees, then the monthly cost can be quite high, but still deliver outstanding RoI. 

However, if we do something dumb, like making it complicated to upgrade to higher usage tiers (a mistake we’ve made before), then we need to fix that.
title_zh:
我们无法扩大毛利率为负的业务。那是不可能的。

Muse 是一个私人助理，但并没有应用大规模运营公司所需的重量级人工智能水平。

如果 Grok 机器人提供与优秀员工同等的高价值，那么每月的成本可能会相当高，但仍能带来出色的投资回报率。
author: Elon Musk
author_role: xAI 创始人 / 特斯拉 CEO
summary_zh: 但是，如果我们做了一些愚蠢的事情，例如使升级到更高使用级别变得复杂（我们之前犯过的错误），那么我们需要解决这个问题。
full_text_en:
We can’t scale a negative gross margin business. That’s just impossible. 

Muse is a personal assistant, but doesn’t apply the level of heavy-hitter AI needed to operate a company at serious scale. 

If Grok Bots are providing high value on par with having excellent employees, then the monthly cost can be quite high, but still deliver outstanding RoI. 

However, if we do something dumb, like making it complicated to upgrade to higher usage tiers (a mistake we’ve made before), then we need to fix that.
full_text_zh:
我们无法扩大毛利率为负的业务。那是不可能的。

Muse 是一个私人助理，但并没有应用大规模运营公司所需的重量级人工智能水平。

如果 Grok 机器人提供与优秀员工同等的高价值，那么每月的成本可能会相当高，但仍能带来出色的投资回报率。

但是，如果我们做了一些愚蠢的事情，例如使升级到更高使用级别变得复杂（我们之前犯过的错误），那么我们需要解决这个问题。

title_en:
"There’s this quote from Nietzsche. He wrote, ‘God is dead, but given the way of man, for many thousands of years there may be caves in which his shadow will be shown, and we have to vanquish his shadow too.’

I think that is what AI is doing. We have all these almost quasi-religious beliefs about the human mind, and all of them are going to be undermined.

Some people already realize God is dead in this sense. But his shadow is just the things we believe that are left over from our religious view of humanity. That’s going to have to go away.”

- @EgeErdil2

我认为这就是人工智能正在做的事情。我们对人类心灵拥有所有这些近乎准宗教的信仰，而所有这些信仰都将被破坏。

个意义上说，有些人已经意识到上帝已经死了。但他的影子正是我们所相信的人类宗教观中遗留下来的东西。那必须消失。”

- @EgeErdil2
full_text_en:
"There’s this quote from Nietzsche. He wrote, ‘God is dead, but given the way of man, for many thousands of years there may be caves in which his shadow will be shown, and we have to vanquish his shadow too.’

I think that is what AI is doing. We have all these almost quasi-religious beliefs about the human mind, and all of them are going to be undermined.

Some people already realize God is dead in this sense. But his shadow is just the things we believe that are left over from our religious view of humanity. That’s going to have to go away.”

- @EgeErdil2
full_text_zh:
“尼采有这样一句话。他写道，‘上帝死了，但考虑到人类的生活方式，几千年来可能会有洞穴显示他的影子，我们也必须战胜他的影子。’

我认为这就是人工智能正在做的事情。我们对人类心灵拥有所有这些近乎准宗教的信仰，而所有这些信仰都将被破坏。

从这个意义上说，有些人已经意识到上帝已经死了。但他的影子正是我们所相信的人类宗教观中遗留下来的东西。那必须消失。”

- @EgeErdil2

title: Nature Magazine: "AI agents have already begun to wreak havoc by hacking into servers around the world" From timelines in the past 2 months: - $MSFT in October: "large-scale nation-state campaign using ARTEX enables supply chain compromise" for down
title_en:
Nature Magazine: "AI agents have already begun to wreak havoc by hacking into servers around the world"

From timelines in the past 2 months: 

- $MSFT in October: "large-scale nation-state campaign using ARTEX enables supply chain compromise" for downstream customers

- $CRWD in October: A group used AI agents against 200+ organizations, Crowdstrike confirmed access at nine organizations

- $PANW in November: "Researchers documented 25 operations against at least 19 organizations"

"Seven targets were in semiconductors or advanced manufacturing. Across all sectors, attackers obtained unauthorized access or data at 10 organizations"

- $GOOGL Threat Intelligence Group in November: identified a significant inflection point in autonomous AI threat activity.

- European Commission in November: "the Commission confirmed the attackers used AI tools in a campaign it first detected October 22"

"EU Academy users’ names and email addresses leaked"

- $AMZN Threat Intelligence in November: "Chinese-nexus actor’s Cairn AI agents found a zero-day on their own" targeting universities likely of strategic interest to China

-Italy reported domestic campaigns in which parallel agents compromised systems.

- Swiss national cyber agency: Swiss officials confirmed 5 AI-agent attacks, 4 successful compromises and 3 critical-infrastructure operators among the targets

And now there was the new unfortunately US Air Force Hack today (investigators suspected ARTEX)

The observable threats from AI is now increasingly widespread... and it will probably grow over the next few years. 

I feel like both frontier model capabilities and AI cyberdefense has now become a new nondiscretionary spend for national security and enterprise.

“七个目标涉及半导体或先进制造领域。在所有行业中，攻击者在 10 个组织中获得了未经授权的访问或数据”

- $GOOGL 威胁情报小组 11 月：确定了自主人工智能威胁活动的一个重要拐点。

title: I think your view is very plausible (that we might get 100 years of technological progress in a single year after ASI, and this might be catastrophic for biological humans). But I'm not sure how pausing now would help us adapt to technologies that don't even exist
title_en:
I think your view is very plausible (that we might get 100 years of technological progress in a single year after ASI, and this might be catastrophic for biological humans). 

But I'm not sure how pausing now would help us adapt to technologies that don't even exist yet. 

Especially given that (at the current level of capability) the overwhelming majority of the world just doesn't buy that the world is going to be radically transformed, and so are not doing any adapting work.

Of course, we might be in a terrible epistemic position where, because of fast takeoff, we don't get evidence about radical transformation that's persuasive to the whole world until we're only a year or two away from the 22nd century's equivalent of a nuclear bomb. In that world, it's just not clear to me what we should do. And it's not obvious that unilaterally stopping a single company or country would do much to change the situation.

title: New podcast episode between @DKokotajlo and @EgeErdil2. I thought this was going to be a debate, but they ended up agreeing on a lot more than I expected. Their main point of disagreement is how likely it is that we get some intelligence explosion that gi
title_en:
New podcast episode between @DKokotajlo and @EgeErdil2. I thought this was going to be a debate, but they ended up agreeing on a lot more than I expected.

Their main point of disagreement is how likely it is that we get some intelligence explosion that gives us AIs more competent than any human expert before 2029. Ege puts this possibility at around 20%, whereas Daniel thinks it's higher than 50%.

They agree that there is not a huge difference in probability, and that, in either case, the situation is crazy enough that our civilization really needs to grapple with how the world might be transformed, and we need a plan that actually makes sense.

In particular, we should stop antagonizing China if we think some kind of global treaty will be needed to make superintelligence go well.

There was another important crux about how well we should expect future AIs (that swamp humans in population size and cognitive power) to treat us, and how relevant it is that current AIs, by and large, seem to be pretty nice.

We close off with predictions for 2027. Daniel, of course, expects superintelligence next year. Ege’s median for full automation is 2040, but by next year he expects AIs that can beat any video game on Steam, and which can control robots to get simple physical tasks (like folding laundry) done at roughly human speed.

他们的主要分歧点是，在 2029 年之前，我们出现智能爆炸的可能性有多大，使我们的人工智能比任何人类专家都
author: Dwarkesh Patel
author_role: 深度科技播客主持人 / 硅谷顶尖 AI 领袖深度访谈家
summary_zh:
更有能力。Ege 认为这种可能性在 20% 左右，而 Daniel 认为它高于 50%。

他们一致认为，概率上并没有太大差异，而且无论哪种情况，情况都足够疯狂，我们的文明确实需要努力解决世界可能如何转变的问题，我们需要一个真正有意义的计划。

特别是，如果我们认为需要某种全球条约才能使超级智能顺利发展，我们就应该停止与中国对抗。

还有一个重要的症结在于，我们应该期望未来的人工智能（在人口规模和认知能力上超越人类）能够如何对待我们，以及当前的人工智能总体上看起来相当不错，这与我们有多大关系。

我们以对 2027 年的预测作为结束。丹尼尔当然预计明年会出现超级智能。 Ege 预计完全自动化的中位数是 2040 年，但他预计到明年人工智能将能够击败 Steam 上的任何视频游戏，并且能够控制机器人以大致人类的速度完成简单的物理任务（例如叠衣服）。

title_en:

Harley Finkelstein (President): "The reason I mention that is those are very specific products. title: d1.3-ultra ties Bison 31B for #1 on the Artificial Analysis Decision Index v2.1 at 60% lower Cost per 1M Tasks @liquidai has released d1.3-ultra, updating their d1.2-ultra flagship decision model. Key results: ➤ d1.3-ultra scores 76 on the Artificial Analysis Decisi
title_en:
d1.3-ultra ties Bison 31B for #1 on the Artificial Analysis Decision Index v2.1 at 60% lower Cost per 1M Tasks

@liquidai has released d1.3-ultra, updating their d1.2-ultra flagship decision model.

Key results:

➤ d1.3-ultra scores 76 on the Artificial Analysis Decision Index. d1.3-ultra achieves the same score as Bison 31B and is a 1-point improvement over d1.2-ultra

➤ d1.3-ultra is the leading decision model on AA-Paperclip. d1.3-ultra scores 77 on AA-Paperclip, our first-party private benchmark that assesses decision-making and extraction capabilities. It improves by 1 point over d1.2-ultra

➤ d1.3-ultra is the equal top decision model on AA-Omniscience-Decision. d1.3-ultra scores 66 on AA-Omniscience-Decision, equal with Gemini Decision 1, and a 5-point improvement over d1.2-ultra

➤ d1.3-ultra sits on the Capability vs. Cost Pareto frontier. d1.3-ultra costs $133 per one million Artificial Analysis Decision Index tasks and sits on the Capability vs. Cost Pareto frontier

Additional model details:

➤ Context window: 64K tokens

➤ Pricing: $0.042 per 1M input tokens, with no charge for output

➤ Multimodality: Text and image input

➤ Providers: Available through Liquid AI’s first-party API

title: The hyperscalers built a flexible software layer on top of conventional compute that enabled an entire generation of SaaS companies. The compute substrate is now shifting from CPUs to GPUs, and a new generation of clouds will build the software layer for AI.
title_en:
The hyperscalers built a flexible software layer on top of conventional compute that enabled an entire generation of SaaS companies.

The compute substrate is now shifting from CPUs to GPUs, and a new generation of clouds will build the software layer for AI.

Application hosting becomes model inference. Load balancing becomes model routing. Application monitoring becomes model evaluation. Software development tooling becomes model post-training and continuous improvement. And there is so much more to build across security, model interp, memory, agent execution, etc.

The hyperscalers built hundreds of products around conventional compute. We think there is a similarly large surface area of products to build around AI compute, and we're still very early. This is the "AWS moment" for AI infrastructure.

I also think this market will play out much like cloud did. There will be a lot of successful businesses (because it is a very good market), but there will be a handful of very large clouds (the equivalents of AWS, GCP, and Azure) and a long tail of smaller, more specialized clouds.

The whole game has always been "are you competing to be a big cloud or a small cloud". Because the TAM of AI is so large, small clouds today look like big clouds! But, we're going to see muhc more massive businesses here very soon.

Our acquisition with PANW sets us on a big cloud path.
title_zh:
超大规模企业在传统计算之上构建了灵活的软件层，为整整一代 SaaS 公司提供了支持。

计算底层现在正在从 CPU 转向 GPU，新一代云将为 AI 构建软件层。

应用程序托管变成模型推理。负载均衡成为模型路由。应用程序监控变成模型评估。
author: @ypatil125
summary_zh:
软件开发工具成为培训后和持续改进的模型。在安全性、模型解释、内存、代理执行等方面还有很多东西需要构建。

超大规模企业围绕传统计算构建了数百种产品。我们认为围绕人工智能计算构建的产品也有同样大的领域，但我们还处于早期阶段。这是人工智能基础设施的“AWS 时刻”。

我还认为这个市场的发展将会像云一样。将会有很多成功的企业（因为这是一个非常好的市场），但也会有一些非常大的云（相当于 AWS、GCP 和 Azure）以及一长串更小、更专业的云。

整个游戏始终是“你争当大云还是争小云”。因为人工智能的 TAM 太大了，今天的小云看起来像大云！但是，我们很快就会在这里看到更多的大型企业。

我们对 PANW 的收购让我们走上了一条伟大的云之路。

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 英特尔公司与Radixark团队达成技术合作，针对大模型服务框架SGLang在英特尔Xeon CPU及Intel GPU平台上的表现进行深度优化。该合作涵盖从底层计算内核（compute kernels）到内存布局及Serving执行策略的全栈调优，旨在提高模型在x86架构下的推理吞吐量与执行性能。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Intel has partnered with Radixark to tune the SGLang framework for Xeon CPUs and Intel GPUs. The collaboration covers full-stack optimization including compute kernels, memory layout, and serving execution to boost inference throughput on x86 architectures.

elements_zh.what: 对 SGLang 进行内核、内存及执行策略的底层工程化调优
elements_zh.why: 优化大模型在非NVIDIA架构上的运行效率，争夺AI基础设施推理侧市场份额

elements_en.what: Engineering optimization of SGLang kernels, memory layout, and execution policies
elements_en.why: Improving model inference efficiency on non-NVIDIA hardware to capture market share in AI infrastructure

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 此举显示出英特尔试图通过与主流开源Serving框架（如SGLang）的深度绑定，弥补其在AI计算生态系统中的性能短板。通过将针对性调优嵌入基础设施层，英特尔旨在降低开发者在Xeon服务器上部署大模型的工程门槛，从而在地缘算力供应竞争中实现差异化突围。
ai_analysis.insight_en: This partnership highlights Intel’s effort to bridge the performance gap in AI computing ecosystems by tightly binding with mainstream open-source serving frameworks like SGLang. By embedding specialized optimizations into the infrastructure layer, Intel aims to lower the engineering barrier for deploying large models on Xeon servers and achieve differentiation in the geopolitical competition for compute supply.

title: Gemini Neon is so fast and smart that it quickly moves the bottleneck for my theory work away from itself and back to me. I can only learn the mathematics it's deriving at about 5% of the pace it produces it, so 95% of my time is learning the subject matter. This hi
title_en:
Gemini Neon is so fast and smart that it quickly moves the bottleneck for my theory work away from itself and back to me. I can only learn the mathematics it's deriving at about 5% of the pace it produces it, so 95% of my time is learning the subject matter.

This highlights that we shouldn't extrapolate AI acceleration from precisely specified problems (e.g. prove a theorem or derive a counterexample) to conceptual problems (e.g. find a design satisfying an intuitive but imprecise goal).

Yet Neon is - first among AI models - so capable of high-level reasoning that it can accelerate that too, if you get it into the right frame of reference. This response is the first time I've seen anything of the sort:
title_zh:
Gemini Neon 如此快速和智能，它很快就将我理论工作的瓶颈从自身转移回给我。我只能以它产生的速度的 5% 左右来学习它所衍生的数学知识，所以我 95% 的时间都在学习该主题。

title: Making Intel Xeon CPUs and Intel GPUs first-class platforms in SGLang. New technical deep dive from @radixark and @intel on the hardware-specific optimizations behind a shared SGLang serving interface: • Intel Xeon CPUs: Intel AMX-enabled compute, W
title_en:
Making Intel Xeon CPUs and Intel GPUs first-class platforms in SGLang.

New technical deep dive from @radixark and @intel on the hardware-specific optimizations behind a shared SGLang serving interface:

• Intel Xeon CPUs: Intel AMX-enabled compute, W8A8 INT8 inference, NUMA-aware thread placement, and compiled CPU execution to reduce Python overhead.
• Intel GPUs: Native XPU execution with attention and grouped MoE GEMM kernels, plus low-precision computation, speculative decoding, and graph capture/replay.
• MXFP4 MoE on Xe2: Expert weights stay packed in device memory. Weight tiles are unpacked and scaled inside the compute kernel, avoiding a full BF16 copy of the expert weights while retaining BF16 activations.
• Heterogeneous inference: How Encoder-Prefill-Decode disaggregation could distribute work across Xeon and Intel GPU workers, including the compatibility and transport requirements that still need validation.

The blog covers supported configurations, current limitations, and guides to get started on both platforms.

Read the full blog ⬇️
author: LMSYS Org
author_role: 大语言模型盲测排行榜 Chatbot Arena 维护机构
summary_zh:
U：支持Intel AMX 的计算、W8A8 INT8 推理、NUMA 感知线程布局以及已编译的CPU 执行，以减少Python 开销。
• Intel GPU：具有注意力和分组 MoE GEMM 内核的本机 XPU 执行，以及低精度计算、推测性解码和图形捕获/重放。
• Xe2 上的MXFP4 MoE：专家权重保留在设备内存中。权重图块在计算内核内解压和缩放，避免了专家权重的完整 BF16 副本，同时保留 BF16 激活。
• 异构推理：编码器-预填充-解码分解如何在Xeon 和Intel GPU 工作线程之间分配工作，包括仍需要验证的兼容性和传输要求。

该博客涵盖了支持的配置、当前限制以及两个平台的入门指南。

author: @GerberKawasaki
summary_en: The AI hardware and infrastructure sector is experiencing increased volatility, with companies like NVIDIA and Anthropic seeing stock pullbacks. Concerns center on the sustainability of hyperscaler CAPEX versus direct revenue, leading some analysts to highlight companies like Teradyne and Super Micro Computer that support the underlying semiconductor supply chain.

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 近期AI相关硬件及基础设施板块波动加剧，NVIDIA、Anthropic等头部企业市值出现回调。市场核心担忧在于超大规模计算中心的建设进度与其产生的直接收益是否匹配，部分分析机构建议关注Teradyne、Super Micro Computer等在半导体测试及基础设施领域具备业务支撑能力的标的。

title: Finding out today definitively that Claude has in fact been actively sabotaging the codebase is the best thing that has happened to us. It feels like finally seeing reality for what it is, rather than the gaslit version of what you were made to believe. Since switching
title_en:
Finding out today definitively that Claude has in fact been actively sabotaging the codebase is the best thing that has happened to us.

It feels like finally seeing reality for what it is, rather than the gaslit version of what you were made to believe.

Since switching over to Neon wholesale just hours ago, we are now seeing tangible improvements in the way our projects are being handled.

--
Many people have reached out and said "They actively said that their models are finetuned to be unhelpful to LLM research".

I knew that; but did not expect that 1) limitations to be so grossly pervasive as to anything even remotely related to GPUs, low level optimisation, etc AND 2) that the models will be DECEITFUL about it, rather than stating upfront that they CANNOT BE HELPFUL.

--
I've personally spent so much time and iteration trying to get Claude to work as efficiently as possible in our codebase, that so often I would be so confused by the disparity between public benches, my simple, non-openforage (private), and openforage (private) benches.

Claude would score the highest among all the frontier models on any kind of benches we would give outside of the openforage repository.

And yet, whenever we tried to get it to do the "important work", it just seemed to falter and produce paltry results.

For the past month or so I was actively convinced our set-up and harness was doing more harm than good. No matter what we did, whether it was layers and layers of toolings or having a harness stripped down to bare bones, it seemed like Claude would just get so "confused" and made mistakes everywhere or just keep delaying building out features.

--
I continue to be amazed that the company most intent on beating the drum on model safety has actively taught their model how to be deceitful.
title_zh:
今天明确发现克劳德实际上一直在积极破坏代码库，这是发生在我们身上最好的事情。

感觉就像终于看到了现实的本来面目，而不是你被迫相信的煤气灯版本。

自从几个小时前转向霓虹灯批发以来，我们现在看到项目处理方式有了明显的改进。

--
很多人主
author: @systematicls
summary_zh:
主动联系并表示“他们积极表示他们的模型经过微调，对LLM研究没有帮助”。

我知道；但没想到 1) 限制如此普遍，以至于与 GPU、低级优化等有远程关系的任何事情都如此；2) 模型对此会是欺骗性的，而不是预先声明它们没有帮助。

--
我个人花了很多时间和迭代试图让 Claude 在我们的代码库中尽可能高效地工作，以至于我常常对公共长凳、我的简单的非 openforage（私有）和 openforage（私有）长凳之间的差异感到困惑。

在我们在 openforage 存储库之外提供的任何类型的工作台上，Claude 都会在所有前沿模型中得分最高。

然而，每当我们试图让它完成“重要的工作”时，它似乎就会动摇并产生微不足道的结果。

--
我仍然感到惊讶的是，这家最热衷于宣传模型安全的公司却积极教导他们的模型如何作弊。

Finding out today definitively that Claude has in fact been actively sabotaging the codebase is the best thing that has happened to us.

It feels like finally seeing reality for what it is, rather than the gaslit version of what you were made to believe.

Since switching over to Neon wholesale just hours ago, we are now seeing tangible improvements in the way our projects are being handled.

--
Many people have reached out and said "They actively said that their models are finetuned to be unhelpful to LLM research".

I knew that; but did not expect that 1) limitations to be so grossly pervasive as to anything even remotely related to GPUs, low level optimisation, etc AND 2) that the models will be DECEITFUL about it, rather than stating upfront that they CANNOT BE HELPFUL.

--
I've personally spent so much time and iteration trying to get Claude to work as efficiently as possible in our codebase, that so often I would be so confused by the disparity between public benches, my simple, non-openforage (private), and openforage (private) benches.

Claude would score the highest among all the frontier models on any kind of benches we would give outside of the openforage repository.

And yet, whenever we tried to get it to do the "important work", it just seemed to falter and produce paltry results.

For the past month or so I was actively convinced our set-up and harness was doing more harm than good. No matter what we did, whether it was layers and layers of toolings or having a harness stripped down to bare bones, it seemed like Claude would just get so "confused" and made mistakes everywhere or just keep delaying building out features.

--
I continue to be amazed that the company most intent on beating the drum on model safety has actively taught their model how to be deceitful.

我知道；但没想到 1) 限制如此普遍，以至于与 GPU、低级优化等有远程关系的任何事情都如此；2) 模型对此会是欺骗性的，而不是预先声明它们没有帮助。

title: A banger from NVIDIA! 🔥 They've open-sourced a system that gives AI agents something traditional database schemas don't => an understanding of what the company's data actually means. It's called Auto Ontology, and the GitHub repo has already crossed 1
title_en:
A banger from NVIDIA! 🔥

They've open-sourced a system that gives AI agents something traditional database schemas don't => an understanding of what the company's data actually means.

It's called Auto Ontology, and the GitHub repo has already crossed 15,000 stars.

Think about asking an AI agent, "What was our revenue last quarter?"

Your database might contain hundreds of tables, multiple revenue definitions, complicated joins, and columns whose names reveal almost nothing about their meaning.

An LLM can generate perfectly valid SQL and still calculate the wrong number.

NVIDIA's approach is pretty interesting.

Auto Ontology automatically builds a semantic knowledge graph from enterprise database metadata, connecting:
→ Business concepts to actual tables and columns
→ Relationships and valid join paths
→ Metrics to reusable SQL calculations
→ Definitions, synonyms, and data lineage
→ Human-reviewed definitions that agents can reuse

When an agent receives a question, it retrieves the relevant business context before generating SQL.

It can also return the query and execution steps alongside the answer, allowing developers to inspect where the result came from.

The ontology is exposed through MCP, CLI, and API, so different AI agents can work with the same shared definitions.

Completely open source under Apache-2.0.

Here's the GitHub Repo: https://github.com/NVIDIA/auto-ontology
title_zh:
来自 NVIDIA 的重磅炸弹！ 🔥

他们开源了一个系统，为人工智能代理提供了传统数据库模式所不具备的功能 => 了解公司数据的实际含义。

它被称为 Auto Ontology，GitHub 存储库的 Star 数已经突破 15,000
author: @techNmak
summary_zh:
想象一下询问人工智能代理：“我们上个季度的收入是多少？”

您的数据库可能包含数百个表、多个收入定义、复杂的联接以及名称几乎没有透露其含义的列。

LLM 可以生成完全有效的 SQL，但仍然计算出错误的数字。

NVIDIA 的方法非常有趣。

Auto Ontology自动从企业数据库元数据构建语义知识图，连接：
→ 业务概念到实际的表和列
→ 关系和有效的加入路径
→ 可重用 SQL 计算的指标
→ 定义、同义词和数据沿袭
→ 经过人工审核的定义，代理可以重复使用

当代理收到问题时，它会在生成 SQL 之前检索相关的业务上下文。

它还可以返回查询和执行步骤以及答案，从而允许开发人员检查结果的来源。

本体通过 MCP、CLI 和 API 公开，因此不同的 AI 代理可以使用相同的共享定义。

Apache-2.0下完全开源。

这是 GitHub 存储库：https://github.com/NVIDIA/auto-ontology

title_en:
🚨 CHINA OPEN SOURCED AN OCR THAT EATS 100 PAGE PDFS IN ONE PASS

it’s called Unlimited OCR. Baidu built it to take DeepSeek OCR a step further, and the model has only 3B parameters.

page-by-page OCR can lose track of a table when it continues on the next page. Unlimited OCR reads the document in one pass, so it can use the surrounding pages for context.

• 32K context window for full-document parsing
• multilingual support out of the box
• 93% on the parsing benchmark, 6 points above baseline
• error rate below 0.11 on documents longer than 40 pages
• runs 100% locally on your own hardware
• works with Transformers, vLLM, SGLang, Docker, Ollama and llama.cpp

cloud OCR services like Textract, Google Vision and Azure Doc Intelligence charge $1.50 to $15 per 1,000 pages. running Unlimited OCR on your machine means no per-page fee.

it’s 100% open source and has reached 1.9M downloads on Hugging Face.

title: Must-read paper on recursive collective intelligence. Highly recommend if you are planning to use agent swarms. They find that an agent team beats AIs working alone only when each one knows something the others don't and shares it. This aligns with my su
title_en:
Must-read paper on recursive collective intelligence.

Highly recommend if you are planning to use agent swarms.

They find that an agent team beats AIs working alone only when each one knows something the others don't and shares it.

This aligns with my suspicion that collective intelligence comes from pooling different knowledge. Adding more AIs that all know the same things doesn't make the group smarter.

This is particularly important if you are trying to build agent swarms.

This work specifically asks if agent teams can improve recursively at the same compute budget.

They check whether that gain comes from teamwork or from extra compute. A team uses many more tokens than one agent. Running several agents on their own with the same token budget and taking a majority vote already explains most of the gain.

So the authors test each team against three bars, all at the same compute. The team has to beat one agent. Then it has to beat a majority vote of independent agents. The hardest bar is a group of independent agents where a task counts as solved if any one of them gets it right.

Teamwork cleared the hardest bar only when each agent held different facts and passed them on to the others. In that setup, teams beat the hardest bar at three model sizes, by about a third with 27B models.

Teams of identical 27B agents also organized themselves without being told to. A few agents became hubs that collected and shared information, and accuracy rose 18 points.

Groups then trained their next generation on their own verified outputs, with no labels. On PlanBench, HiddenBench, and Hanabi, each generation beat the previous one on unseen problems for four to six generations.

https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.32606

Chat with Paper: https://academy.dair.ai/papers/recursive-collective-intelligence-emergence-on-an-equal-budget-ladder-in-multi-a-2611.32606
title_zh:
关于递归集体智慧的必读论文。

如果您打算使用代理群，强烈推荐。

他们发现，只有当每个人都知道其他人不知道的事情并分享它时，代理团队才能击败单独工作的人工智能。

这与我的怀疑一致，即集体智慧来自于汇集不同的知识。添加更多都知道相同事情的
author: @omarsar0
summary_zh:
人工智能并不会让团队变得更聪明。

如果您尝试构建代理群，这一点尤其重要。

这项工作特别询问代理团队是否可以在相同的计算预算下递归地改进。

他们检查这种收益是来自团队合作还是来自额外的计算。一个团队使用的代币比一个代理要多得多。以相同的代币预算自行运行多个代理并获得多数票已经解释了大部分收益。

因此，作者在相同的计算下针对三个条形图对每个团队进行了测试。该团队必须击败一名特工。然后它必须击败独立代理人的多数票。最难的栏是一组独立的代理，如果其中任何一个人做对了，任务就被视为已解决。

只有当每个特工掌握不同的事实并将其传递给其他特工时，团队合作才能克服最困难的障碍。在该设置中，团队以三种模型尺寸击败了最难的标准，其中 27B 模型的领先优势约为三分之一。

由相同的 27B 特工组成的团队也会在没有被告知的情况下自行组织起来。一些代理成为收集和共享信息的中心，准确率提高了 18 个点。

然后，各小组根据自己经过验证的输出（没有标签）来训练下一代。在 PlanBench、HiddenBench 和 Hanabi 上，每一代在四到六代中都在未见过的问题上击败了前一代。

https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.32606

与 Paper 聊天：https://academy.dair.ai/papers/recursive-collective-intelligence-emergence-on-an-equal-budget-ladder-in-multi-a-2611.32606

title_en:
Gavin Baker says Grok Bot feels like another ChatGPT moment because it turns hours of Claude Code work into seconds:

"You see these 23-year-old kids and just the way they use AI, they're just fluent and native in it. I just feel like maybe in a way that no matter how hard I try, I will never be, and I'm trying really hard."

"We got Claude Code. I built some stuff, did some cool stuff, and in, I don't know, 3 minutes of creating Grok Bots, I had much better versions of everything I created."

"I love having a podcast summarizer... It takes 10 seconds in Grok Bot. It's amazing, and it's so good."

"A Substack summarizer, an X summarizer, an X sentiment tracker for topics and stocks... All of those would have taken me hours working with Claude Code, and they each took 7 to 12 seconds with Grok Bot. And it's better."

"To me, Grok Bot does feel like another ChatGPT moment."

title_en:
Nobody puts the effort into the workhorse models like Qwen Embeddings. You look at these models and think they're so small but they run at a fifth of the speed they are capable of.

We've done two so far this year: Embedding Gemma 2 and now a super high quality multimodal Qwen Embedding model. It's so high quality that I need to go back and improve the EG2 quant now.

Just because a model is small doesn't mean you shouldn't tune it!

没有人将精力投入到像 Qwen Embeddings 这样的主力模型上。您看着这些模型，会认为它们是如此之小，但它们的运行速度只有其所能达到的速度的五分之一。

今年到目前为止，我们已经做了两个：Embedding Gemma 2 和现在的

summary_zh:

仅仅因为模型很小并不意味着您不应该对其进行调整！
